claims.quote: For he said that the sacred strength of Balder's body was proof even against steel; adding, however, that he knew of a sword which could deal him his death, which was fastened up in the closest bonds; this was in the keeping of Miming, the Satyr of the woods, who also had a bracelet of a secret and marvellous virtue, that used to increase the wealth of the owner.

statement.id: Gewar berkata bahwa kekuatan suci tubuh Balder kebal bahkan terhadap baja, tetapi ia tahu sebuah pedang yang dapat membunuhnya, terikat sangat ketat dan disimpan oleh Miming, Satir hutan, yang juga memiliki gelang berkhasiat rahasia yang menambah kekayaan pemiliknya.
statement.en: Gewar said that the sacred strength of Balder's body was proof even against steel, but he knew of a sword that could kill him, tightly bound and kept by Miming, the Satyr of the woods, who also had a bracelet of secret virtue that increased its owner's wealth.

claims.quote: So he advised him to harness a car with reindeer, by means of whose great speed he could cross the hard-frozen ridges. And when he had got to the place, he should set up his tent away from the sun in such wise that it should catch the shadow of the cave where Miming was wont to be

statement.id: Gewar menasihati Hother memakai kereta rusa kutub agar cepat melintasi punggung bukit yang membeku, lalu mendirikan tenda membelakangi matahari sehingga terkena bayangan gua tempat Miming biasa tinggal.
statement.en: Gewar advised Hother to harness a reindeer car to cross the frozen ridges quickly, then pitch his tent away from the sun so it caught the shadow of the cave where Miming used to be.

claims.quote: when the Satyr cast a shadow on his tent. Aiming a spear at him, he brought him down with the blow, stopped him, and bound him, while he could not make his escape. Then in the most dreadful words he threatened him with the worst, and demanded the sword and bracelets. The Satyr was not slow to tender him the ransom of his life for which he was asked.

statement.id: Ketika satir itu melemparkan bayangan ke tendanya, Hother menjatuhkannya dengan lembing dan mengikatnya, mengancamnya, dan menuntut pedang serta gelang; satir itu segera menyerahkan tebusan nyawanya.
statement.en: When the Satyr cast a shadow on his tent, Hother brought him down with a spear and bound him, threatened him and demanded the sword and bracelets; the Satyr promptly gave the ransom for his life.

claims.quote: These Saxo calls Satyrs, and but rarely mentions. The dwarf Miming, who lives in the desert, has a precious sword of sharpness (Mistletoe?) that could even pierce skin-hard Balder, and a ring (Draupnir) that multiplied itself for its possessor.

statement.id: Dalam pengantar terjemahan, kurcaci disebut Saxo sebagai satir dan jarang disinggung; kurcaci Miming yang tinggal di tempat sunyi memiliki pedang tajam berharga yang bahkan bisa menembus kulit keras Balder, serta cincin (Draupnir) yang melipatgandakan dirinya bagi pemiliknya.
statement.en: In the translator's introduction, dwarfs are what Saxo calls Satyrs and rarely mentions; the dwarf Miming, living in the wilds, has a precious keen sword able to pierce even skin-hard Balder and a ring (Draupnir) that multiplied itself for its owner.

claims.quote: Nella mitologia norrena, Miming era un troll che abitava nella foresta, era il figlio di Hothbrod e l'allievo di Gevar. In una versione teutonica del mito della morte di Baldr, la spada di Miming è l'arma che Höðr usa per uccidere Baldr.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, dalam mitologi Nordik Miming adalah troll penghuni hutan, putra Hothbrod dan murid Gevar; dalam satu versi Teutonik mitos kematian Baldr, pedang Miming adalah senjata yang dipakai Höðr untuk membunuh Baldr.
statement.en: According to the Italian article, Miming in Norse mythology was a forest-dwelling troll, son of Hothbrod and pupil of Gevar; in a Teutonic version of Baldr's death myth, Miming's sword is the weapon Höðr uses to kill Baldr.

short_description.id: Mistapew adalah makhluk roh yang dikenal luas dalam kebudayaan masyarakat tutur Cree-Montagnais-Naskapi [mistapew-c01].
short_description.en: Mistapew is a spirit-being found widely in cultures across the Cree-Montagnais-Naskapi language continuum [mistapew-c01].

long_description.id: Mistapew (juga Mista´peo, Mištapew, atau Mishtapew) adalah makhluk roh yang dikenal luas dalam kebudayaan rumpun bahasa Cree-Montagnais-Naskapi. Namanya gabungan misti- ("besar, agung") dan nâpêw ("lelaki"), sehingga berarti "lelaki besar"; ejaan lain Mistabeo diartikan "lelaki agung, roh penolong".
long_description.en: Mistapew (also Mista´peo, Mištapew or Mishtapew) is a spirit-being found widely in the cultures of the Cree-Montagnais-Naskapi language continuum. The name joins misti- ("big, great") and nâpêw ("man"), meaning "big man"; the variant spelling Mistabeo is glossed "great man, spirit-helper".

long_description.id: Menurut penelitian Flannery, Mištapew bukan roh milik pemburu sendiri, melainkan sekutu roh yang dapat dijumpai dan dimintai kebijaksanaan. Peran utamanya ada dalam Upacara Tenda Bergoyang, sebagai pemandu yang memperkenalkan roh-roh dan menafsirkan pesan mereka. Kekuatannya boleh diterima atau ditolak, dan dapat dipakai untuk meramal, mengalahkan Atush, atau untuk sihir.
long_description.en: According to Flannery's research, Mištapew was not a hunter's own spirit but a spirit ally who could be met and asked for wisdom. His main role was in the Shaking Tent Rite, as the master of ceremonies who introduced the spirits and interpreted their messages. His power could be accepted or refused, and could be used to foretell, to overcome the Atush, or for sorcery.

long_description.id: Mistapew digambarkan memperluas kemampuan manusia hanya sampai batas tertentu: ia melihat masa depan lebih baik daripada manusia tetapi bisa keliru, dan dapat membunuh karibu dengan cepat. Ia tetap memandu upacara tenda bergoyang yang terakhir dilakukan di Rupert House pada 1965. Di bawah pengaruh misi Kristen, sebagian orang menganggap Tuhan Kristen pengganti Mistabeo yang lebih kuat, sementara yang lain menerima anggapan misionaris bahwa Mistabeo perwujudan Iblis.
long_description.en: Mistapew is described as extending human abilities only so far: he sees the future better than people but may be wrong, and can kill caribou quickly. He remained master of ceremonies in the shaking tent, last performed at Rupert House in 1965. Under missionary influence some people took the Christian God as a stronger replacement for Mistabeo, while others accepted the missionaries' view of Mistabeo as the Devil's manifestation.

long_description.id: Tradisi lain memberi gambaran berbeda. Dalam kisah bintang Cree, mistapew adalah raksasa yang memperdagangkan roh dan menyusup ke mimpi tujuh bersaudara untuk mengambil roh mereka. Para tetua penutur Cree menyebut Mistapew atau Sabe sebagai guru kejujuran yang berdiam di sisi tak kasatmata dunia dan sering disebut "Bigfoot". Speck mencatat bahwa dalam beberapa cerita Mistapew dapat memakan manusia, sehingga ia melihat kemiripannya dengan Witigo.
long_description.en: Other traditions give different pictures. In a Cree star story the mistapew is a giant who trades in spirits and creeps into the dreams of seven brothers to take their spirits. Cree-speaking elders speak of Mistapew or Sabe as the teacher of honesty dwelling in the unseen aspects of the world, often called "Bigfoot". Speck noted that in some stories Mistapew can eat humans, and so saw a likeness to the Witigo.

long_description.id: Kisah-kisah tentang Mistapew masih hidup dalam budaya tradisional dan populer masyarakat adat Amerika Utara pada abad ke-21.
long_description.en: Mistapew stories are still told today, both in traditional settings and in Indigenous North American popular culture.

short_description.id: Mo-sin-a adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Taiwan berbentuk manusia pendek berbulu.
short_description.en: Mo-sin-a is a Taiwanese folkloric creature portrayed as short and hairy with a human-like form.

long_description.id: Mo-sin-a adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Taiwan berbentuk manusia pendek berbulu. Kisah menempatkannya di hutan pegunungan dan mengaitkannya dengan pengalihan orang ke tempat terpencil. Surat kabar masa Jepang menyebut makhluk ini beberapa kali.
long_description.en: Mo-sin-a is a Taiwanese folkloric creature portrayed as short and hairy with a human-like form. Accounts place it in mountain forests and link it with luring people into remote places. Japanese-period newspapers mention this creature several times.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah wawancara dengan peneliti, 魔神仔 digambarkan sebagai siluman gunung dan air yang bertubuh kecil, dapat berubah rupa, dan suka mengusili orang. Gadis Kecil Berbaju Merah dan 玉山黃色小飛俠 disebut sebagai jenis-jenisnya. Dalam kisahnya, orang yang dibawa pergi ditemukan di pohon atau gua, dan 魔神仔 meminta pakaian dari orang; bila seseorang hilang di pegunungan, orang berteriak memanggil namanya. Peneliti itu membedakannya dari hantu, yang kisahnya muncul setelah seseorang meninggal di suatu tempat.
long_description.en: In an interview with a researcher, the 魔神仔 is described as a mountain or water spirit-monster that is small, able to transform, and fond of playing tricks on people. The Little Girl in Red and the 玉山黃色小飛俠 are said to be kinds of it. In its stories, people who are taken away are found in trees or caves, and the 魔神仔 ask people for clothes; when someone goes missing in the mountains, people call out the name of the person taken. The researcher distinguishes it from ghosts, whose stories arise after someone has died in a place.

long_description.id: Peneliti itu menilai kisah 魔神仔 sebagai warisan budaya yang layak dimanfaatkan untuk mengenalkan budaya Taiwan. Penulis skenario film horor 《紅衣小女孩》 juga menyatakan terinspirasi oleh kelas dan buku peneliti tersebut.
long_description.en: The researcher regards 魔神仔 stories as cultural heritage worth using to introduce Taiwan's culture. The screenwriter of the horror film 《紅衣小女孩》 also said he was inspired by that researcher's class and book.

cultural_context.id: Peneliti 林美容 berpendapat bahwa kisah-kisah 魔神仔 semestinya diperlakukan sebagai warisan budaya dan dimanfaatkan sebagai bahan lokal agar orang mengenal budaya Taiwan.
cultural_context.en: The researcher 林美容 holds that 魔神仔 legends should be treated as cultural heritage and used as local material to help people know Taiwan's culture.

claims.quote: 例如，在樹上或是洞穴發現被魔神仔帶走的人，這可以連結到早期人類的叢林生活經驗；而魔神仔跟人要衣服穿，則是與人類文明的進展相關，是一種羞恥心的展現。

statement.en: When someone is "spirited away" (神隱) in the mountains, people call out the name of the person taken by the 魔神仔; the researcher likens this naming to humans passing from nameless to named.

statement.en: The 魔神仔 plays tricks on people in the wild, whereas ghost stories arise after someone has died in a place, so the two are distinguished.

statement.en: The screenwriter of the Taiwanese horror film 《紅衣小女孩》, 簡士耕, said he was inspired to write it after taking 林美容's class and reading 《魔神仔的人類學想像》.

statement.id: 林美容 berpendapat bahwa masyarakat Taiwan semestinya memperlakukan kisah-kisah 魔神仔 sebagai warisan budaya dan memakainya sebagai bahan lokal agar orang mengenal budaya Taiwan.
statement.en: 林美容 holds that Taiwanese society should treat 魔神仔 legends as cultural heritage and use these spirits as local material to help people know Taiwan's culture.

short_description.id: Moehau (juga maeroero) adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Selandia Baru yang dikatakan tinggal di Moehau, Semenanjung Coromandel, dan dikaitkan dengan maero, manusia liar hutan.
short_description.en: The moehau (also maeroero) is a creature of New Zealand folklore said to dwell on Moehau in the Coromandel Peninsula, and is linked by some to the maero, wild men of the forest.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Selandia Baru, moehau (juga disebut maeroero) adalah makhluk yang dikatakan tinggal di Moehau, Semenanjung Coromandel di North Island. Sebagian orang Māori menduga makhluk itu keturunan maero, yang kadang digambarkan sebagai raksasa atau manusia liar hutan.
long_description.en: Folklore from New Zealand tells of the moehau, known too as the maeroero, a being reputed to live on Moehau on the Coromandel Peninsula of the North Island. Some Māori propose that it is descended from the maero, whom people sometimes picture as giants or wild men of the woods.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Māori, maero adalah bangsa supernatural yang digambarkan liar, jahat, sering kasar, membawa gada batu, dan berbulu tubuh gelap. Sebuah artikel majalah AA Directions menyebut moehau (atau maeroero) sebagai makhluk besar berkaki dua yang berbulu lebat dan mengaitkannya dengan gunung Moehau yang keramat bagi Marutūāhu.
long_description.en: In Māori tradition the maero are a supernatural people portrayed as wild, malevolent and often violent, carrying stone clubs and covered in dark body hair. An AA Directions magazine article describes the moehau (or maeroero) as a large bipedal creature covered in a thick coat of hair and ties it to Mount Moehau, sacred to the Marutūāhu.

long_description.id: Penjelasan lain menyebut moehau sebagai laporan berlebihan tentang gorila atau babon yang lolos, tetapi George Dean, Direktur Kebun Binatang Auckland, membantah teori babon. Pada 1970, Jim Reedy mengatakan bahwa Moehau Berbulu adalah pembesar-besaran dari sebuah lelucon, dan Bob Grey mengatakan istilah Moehau Monster berasal dari nama sebuah Yankee steam hauler untuk menebang kayu.
long_description.en: Another explanation holds that the moehau was an exaggerated report of an escaped gorilla or baboon, but George Dean, Director of Auckland Zoo, refuted the baboon theory. In 1970 Jim Reedy said the Hairy Moehau was an exaggeration from a joke, and Bob Grey said the term Moehau Monster came from the name of a Yankee steam hauler used for logging.

short_description.id: Mogwai adalah transliterasi istilah Kanton untuk monster, roh jahat, setan, atau iblis.
short_description.en: Mogwai transliterates a Cantonese term for monsters, evil spirits, devils, or demons.

long_description.id: Mogwai adalah transliterasi istilah Kanton untuk monster, roh jahat, setan, atau iblis. Unsur mo dihubungkan dengan kata Sanskerta māra.
long_description.en: Mogwai transliterates a Cantonese term for monsters, evil spirits, devils, or demons. The mo element is linked to Sanskrit māra.

long_description.id: Wiktionary menjelaskan bahwa 魔 adalah pemendekan dari 魔羅 yang berasal dari kata Sanskerta māra, dan mencatat arti 魔 antara lain mara dalam Buddhisme, iblis, roh jahat, serta hal atau orang yang jahat. Untuk 魔鬼, kamus yang sama memberi arti iblis, setan, makhluk jahat, atau perwujudan kejahatan. Mogui juga dapat dibedakan dari yaoguai dan dari gui (hantu).
long_description.en: Wiktionary explains that 魔 is a clipping of 魔羅 from the Sanskrit māra, and records meanings of 魔 including mara in Buddhism, devil, evil spirit, and an evil thing or person. For 魔鬼 the same dictionary gives devil, demon, fiend, or an embodiment of evil. Mogui can also be distinguished from yaoguai and from gui (ghosts).

long_description.id: Rakshasa dan yaksha diberikan sebagai contoh iblis Tiongkok yang berasal dari cerita rakyat India. Rakshasa digambarkan sebagai pemakan manusia bertubuh besar yang mampu terbang cepat dan menakutkan, sedangkan yaksha penjelajah udara digambarkan sebagai penerbang malam bersayap sepasang. Catatan kaki dalam terjemahan kumpulan cerita Tionghoa juga menyebut yakcha sebagai iblis yang memakan daging manusia.
long_description.en: The rakshasa and yaksha are given as examples of Chinese demons that derive from Indian folklore. The rakshasa are described as large man-eaters capable of swift and terrifying flight, while air-traversing yaksha are depicted as night flyers with one pair of wings. A footnote in a translation of Chinese tales also describes yakcha as demons who feed upon human flesh.

description.en: Rakshasa are described as capable of swift and terrifying flight, and air-traversing yaksha are described as flying through the night with a pair of wings.

short_description.id: Mohan (juga Muan, Moan, atau Poira) adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Colombia, sering digambarkan sebagai sosok bertubuh besar berambut lebat yang menghuni sungai dan gua di tepi air.
short_description.en: The Mohan (also Muan, Moan or Poira) is a supernatural being of Colombian folklore, often described as a large, heavily haired figure haunting rivers and waterside caves.

long_description.id: Nama Muan, Moan, atau Mohan, yang kadang juga disebut Poira, dipakai untuk beberapa makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Selatan dan Tengah. Penggunaannya yang paling umum merujuk pada arwah orang mati dan leluhur pribumi masa lampau. Banyak legendanya berasal dari Colombia, tempat Mohan juga bisa berarti roh hutan atau tanah tandus.
long_description.en: The names Muan, Moan or Mohan, sometimes also Poira, are applied to several supernatural beings of South and Central American folklore. In its most frequent sense, the word denotes the spirits of the deceased and of ancient native forebears. Many of its legends come from Colombia, where Mohan can also mean a forest or barren-land spirit.

long_description.id: Mohán digambarkan sebagai manusia bertubuh sangat besar dengan rambut panjang, lebat, dan kusut yang menutupi sebagian besar tubuhnya. Ia dikatakan berkeliaran di gua dekat anak sungai, sungai, atau laguna dan bisa dijumpai pada malam hari di dekat sungai. Ia termasuk tokoh mitologis paling representatif di bekas Estado Soberano del Tolima, yang meliputi Tolima dan Huila.
long_description.en: The Mohán is described as a very large human whose long, thick, unkempt hair covers most of its body. It is said to roam caves near streams, rivers or lagoons and to be found at night near the river. It is among the most representative mythological figures of the former Estado Soberano del Tolima, comprising Tolima and Huila.

long_description.id: Kisahnya beragam. Dalam sebagian legenda Mohan adalah makhluk mirip satir yang menculik perempuan muda dan menyimpan mereka di gua di dasar sungai besar; dalam legenda lain ia mencuri umpan, tangkapan, atau jala nelayan dan dapat berubah menjadi binatang mirip kucing. Di Tolima ia dikisahkan bepergian dengan rakit, mengisap tembakau untuk mengusir serangga, dan menjelma menjadi manusia untuk membeli aguardiente. Dalam versi regional lain ia dianggap dewa perairan dan sungai.
long_description.en: The tales vary. In some legends the Mohan is a satyr-like being that steals young women and keeps them in a grotto at the bottom of great rivers; in others it steals fishermen's bait, catch or nets and can change into a cat-like beast. In Tolima it is said to travel by raft, smoke tobacco to drive away insects, and take human form to buy aguardiente. Another regional version regards it as a deity of the waters and rivers.

long_description.id: Mohan juga dikenal sebagai wujud yang dapat diambil oleh dukun. Satu mitos menceritakan seorang dukun yang menjadi aligator agar bisa dekat dengan gadis-gadis yang bermain di sungai. Poira, yang namanya dapat dipertukarkan dengan Mohan, oleh sebagian orang digambarkan sebagai penyihir pribumi yang tinggal di Cerro del Pacandé di Tolima.
long_description.en: The Mohan is also known as a form that shamans can adopt. One myth tells of a shaman who became an alligator to be close to girls playing in the river. Some accounts treat Poira as another name for the same figure and picture it as a native sorcerer dwelling on the Cerro del Pacandé in Tolima.

short_description.id: Mokosh adalah dewi Slavia yang menurut rekonstruksi berhubungan dengan air dan kesuburan; ia satu-satunya dewi yang tercatat dalam jajaran dewa Kiev.
short_description.en: Mokosh is a Slavic goddess whom reconstructions link with waters and fertility; she was among the gods whose statues stood in Kiev.

long_description.id: Mokosh adalah dewi Slavia yang kisahnya tidak bertahan. Namanya muncul dalam khotbah-khotbah anti-pagan bersama para vila, tetapi tanpa penjelasan, sehingga semua gambaran modern tentangnya merupakan hasil rekonstruksi. Satu sumber menyebutnya, bersama dewi Polabia Siva, sebagai satu-satunya dewi Slavia yang terbukti secara historis, seorang dewi ibu yang mengurus kesuburan, kewanitaan, serta perlindungan domba, pemintalan, dan tenun.
long_description.en: Mokosh is a Slavic goddess whose myths have not survived. Her name appears in sermons against paganism alongside the vilas, but without description, so every modern picture of her is a reconstruction. One source counts her, together with the Polabian goddess Siva, as the only historically attested Slavic goddess, a mother goddess in charge of fertility, womanhood and the protection of sheep, spinning and weaving.

long_description.id: Mokosh termasuk enam dewa yang patungnya didirikan oleh Pangeran Vladimir I di Kiev pada tahun 980, sehingga ia tergolong dewa utama bangsa Slavia Timur. Dalam sumber tertulis ia biasanya disebut bersama roh-roh air, yakni vila dan kemudian rusalka. Setelah Kristenisasi, perlindungan ladang dan ternak yang dulu menjadi urusannya dialihkan kepada Santa Paraskeva, namun pada abad ke-16 perempuan masih ditanya dalam pengakuan dosa apakah mereka pergi kepada Mokosh.
long_description.en: Mokosh was one of six deities whose statues Prince Vladimir I set up in Kiev in 980, making her one of the chief gods of the East Slavs. Written sources usually mention her with water spirits, the vilas and later the rusalkas. After Christianisation the protection of fields and livestock that had been hers passed to Saint Paraskeva, yet in the 16th century women were still asked at confession whether they went to Mokosh.

long_description.id: Nama Mokosh paling umum dijelaskan berasal dari akar Proto-Slavia *mok- yang berarti "basah", sehingga ia dipahami sebagai "dia yang basah". Dari situ ia direkonstruksi sebagai dewi air dan kesuburan, yang kemudian tercermin dalam sosok Mat Zemlya, personifikasi Bumi dalam cerita rakyat Slavia Timur, dan dilambangkan sebagai "Ibu Bumi yang lembap" yang sepadan dengan dewi Iran Ardvi Sur Anahita.
long_description.en: The most widely accepted explanation derives Mokosh from the Proto-Slavic stem *mok-, "wet", so that she is understood as "She who is wet". On that basis she is reconstructed as a goddess of waters and fertility, later reflected in Mat Zemlya, the personification of Earth in East Slavic folklore, and symbolised as the "moist Mother Earth" corresponding to the Iranian goddess Ardvi Sur Anahita.

long_description.id: Rekonstruksi lain bertumpu pada catatan etnografi: pada akhir abad ke-19, kikimora di Rusia Utara disebut Mokusha atau Mokosha, dan kikimora dianggap versi dewi ini yang telah dijadikan iblis. Hingga abad ke-19 dikenal pula iblis perempuan bernama Mokusch, berkepala besar dan bertangan panjang, yang datang ke rumah petani pada malam hari untuk memintal serat yang tergeletak. Dari sini para peneliti menggambarkan Mokosh sebagai dewi cinta dan kelahiran yang terkait dengan malam, bulan, pemintalan, peternakan domba, dan urusan rumah tangga perempuan, meski data etimologi menunjukkan pemintalan tidak mungkin menjadi peran utamanya.
long_description.en: Another reconstruction rests on ethnography: at the end of the 19th century the kikimora was called Mokusha or Mokosha in the Russian North, and the kikimora is seen as a demonised version of the goddess. Until the 19th century there was also a female demon called Mokusch, with a big head and long hands, who came to peasant houses at night to spin loose fibre. From this, researchers portrayed Mokosh as a goddess of love and birth tied to night, the moon, spinning, sheep farming and women's economy, though etymological data show spinning could not have been her main role.

statement.en: By etymological reconstruction Mokosh was a goddess of waters and fertility; most researchers say she was later reflected in bylinas and zagovory as Mat Zemlya, the personification of Earth in East Slavic folklore.

claims.quote: at the end of the 19th century, the names kikimora as Mokusha or Mokosha were recorded in the Russian North. The coincidence is explained by kikimora being a demonized version of the goddess

statement.id: Pada akhir abad ke-19, di Rusia Utara tercatat nama kikimora sebagai Mokusha atau Mokosha; kesamaan ini dijelaskan dengan menganggap kikimora versi dewi ini yang dijadikan iblis.
statement.en: At the end of the 19th century kikimora was recorded as Mokusha or Mokosha in the Russian North; this is explained by the kikimora being a demonised version of the goddess.

claims.quote: researchers have portrayed Mokosh as the goddess of love and birth, with a connection to night, the moon, spinning, sheep farming and women's economy.

statement.id: Para peneliti menggambarkan Mokosh sebagai dewi cinta dan kelahiran yang terkait dengan malam, bulan, pemintalan, peternakan domba, dan ekonomi perempuan.
statement.en: Researchers have portrayed Mokosh as a goddess of love and birth, linked with night, the moon, spinning, sheep farming and women's economy.

claims.quote: This reconstruction disagrees with data on her etymology, which shows spinning could not have been the deity's main role.

statement.id: Rekonstruksi ini bertentangan dengan data etimologi, yang menunjukkan pemintalan tidak mungkin menjadi peran utama sang dewi.
statement.en: This reconstruction conflicts with the etymological data, which show spinning could not have been her main role.

claims.quote: based on ethnographic and linguistic data, depicts Mokosh as Perun's wife. It is believed Mokosh cheated on Perun with Veles, causing Perun to kill Mokosh's children. The theory has not been recognized in academia.

statement.id: Versi Slavia dari teori mitos dasar menggambarkan Mokosh sebagai istri Perun yang berselingkuh dengan Veles sehingga Perun membunuh anak-anak Mokosh; teori ini tidak diakui kalangan akademik.
statement.en: The Slavic version of the basic myth theory depicts Mokosh as Perun's wife who cheated on him with Veles, so Perun killed her children; the theory is not recognised in academia.

claims.quote: According to the most-reasonable and widespread etymology the theonym was formed by the suffixal method from the Proto-Slavic stem *mok- meaning "wet" with the suffix *-ošь. Vladimir Toporov and Vyacheslav Ivanov comment this etymology is "indisputable", understanding her name as "She who is wet".

statement.id: Menurut etimologi yang paling masuk akal dan tersebar luas, nama ini dibentuk dari akar Proto-Slavia *mok- "basah" dengan akhiran *-ošь; Vladimir Toporov dan Vyacheslav Ivanov menganggapnya tak terbantahkan dan mengartikan namanya "dia yang basah".
statement.en: By the most reasonable and widespread etymology the name was formed from the Proto-Slavic stem *mok- "wet" with the suffix *-ošь; Vladimir Toporov and Vyacheslav Ivanov call this indisputable, reading the name as "She who is wet".

claims.quote: In Old East Slavic texts, the name Mokosh is rendered as Mokošĭ ( мокошь ), Mokŭšĭ ( мокъшь )

statement.id: Dalam teks Slavia Timur Kuno, nama Mokosh ditulis Mokošĭ (мокошь) dan Mokŭšĭ (мокъшь).
statement.en: In Old East Slavic texts the name Mokosh is written Mokošĭ (мокошь) and Mokŭšĭ (мокъшь).

claims.quote: Mokosh, unlike Macha, was not a warrior, but from the 16th century her name was used to refer to witches and healers, indicating a possible function as a prophetess.

statement.id: Berbeda dengan Macha, Mokosh bukan pejuang, tetapi sejak abad ke-16 namanya dipakai untuk menyebut penyihir dan penyembuh, yang menandakan kemungkinan fungsi sebagai peramal.
statement.en: Unlike Macha, Mokosh was not a warrior, but from the 16th century her name was used for witches and healers, suggesting a possible role as a prophetess.

claims.quote: Celtologist Viktor Kalygin approximated Mokosh to the Irish goddess Macha, in his opinion originally the goddess of fertility.

statement.id: Ahli Kelt Viktor Kalygin menyamakan Mokosh dengan dewi Irlandia Macha, yang menurutnya semula dewi kesuburan.
statement.en: Celtologist Viktor Kalygin likened Mokosh to the Irish goddess Macha, originally in his view a fertility goddess.

claims.quote: Sie ist neben der polabischen Göttin Siva die einzige bekannte historisch belegbare weibliche Gottheit des slawischen Pantheons und als Muttergöttin zuständig für Fruchtbarkeit, Weiblichkeit und den Schutz der Schafe und des Spinnens und Webens.

statement.id: Bersama dewi Polabia Siva, Mokosh (Mokosch) adalah satu-satunya dewi yang terbukti secara historis dalam jajaran dewa Slavia, dan sebagai dewi ibu ia mengurus kesuburan, kewanitaan, serta perlindungan domba, pemintalan, dan tenun.
statement.en: With the Polabian goddess Siva, Mokosh (Mokosch) is the only historically attested female deity of the Slavic pantheon, and as mother goddess she oversees fertility, womanhood and the protection of sheep, spinning and weaving.

claims.quote: Mokosch war eine der sechs Gottheiten, denen Fürst Vladimir I. 980 in Kiew Standbilder aufstellen ließ. Sie zählte also zu den Hauptgöttern der Ostslawen.

statement.id: Mokosh termasuk enam dewa yang patungnya didirikan Pangeran Vladimir I di Kiev (Kiew) pada tahun 980, sehingga ia tergolong dewa utama Slavia Timur.
statement.en: Mokosh was one of six deities for whom Prince Vladimir I set up statues in Kiev (Kiew) in 980, so she was one of the chief gods of the East Slavs.

claims.quote: Nach der Christianisierung wurde der Schutz der Felder und des Viehs, der Mokosch oblag, der Heiligen Paraskeva übertragen.

statement.id: Setelah Kristenisasi, perlindungan ladang dan ternak yang menjadi tugas Mokosh dialihkan kepada Santa Paraskeva.
statement.en: After Christianisation the protection of fields and livestock that had been Mokosh's task passed to Saint Paraskeva.

claims.quote: Doch noch im 16. Jahrhundert wurden Frauen bei der Beichte gefragt, ob sie zu Mokosch gingen

statement.id: Pada abad ke-16 perempuan masih ditanya dalam pengakuan dosa apakah mereka pergi kepada Mokosh.
statement.en: In the 16th century women were still asked at confession whether they went to Mokosh.

claims.quote: bis zum 19. Jahrhundert hielt sich in der nordrussischen und ukrainischen Folklore die Vorstellung eines weiblichen Dämons namens Mokusch, mit großem Kopf und langen Händen, der nachts in die Bauernhäuser kam und das Werg spann, das offen herumlag

statement.id: Hingga abad ke-19, cerita rakyat Rusia Utara dan Ukraina mengenal iblis perempuan bernama Mokusch, berkepala besar dan bertangan panjang, yang datang ke rumah petani pada malam hari dan memintal serat yang tergeletak.
statement.en: Until the 19th century North Russian and Ukrainian folklore knew a female demon called Mokusch, with a big head and long hands, who came to peasant houses at night and spun loose fibre.

claims.quote: In den schriftlichen Quellen wird sie meist zusammen mit Wassergeistern erwähnt, den Vilen, später den Rusalken.

statement.id: Dalam sumber tertulis Mokosh biasanya disebut bersama roh air, yaitu vila (Vilen) dan kemudian rusalka (Rusalken).
statement.en: In written sources she is usually mentioned together with water spirits, the vilas (Vilen) and later the rusalkas (Rusalken).

claims.quote: Sie symbolisiert demnach die „feuchte Mutter Erde“ und entspricht damit der iranischen Fruchtbarkeitsgöttin Ardvi Sur Anahita.

statement.id: Karena itu Mokosh melambangkan "Ibu Bumi yang lembap" dan sepadan dengan dewi kesuburan Iran Ardvi Sur Anahita.
statement.en: She thus symbolises the "moist Mother Earth" and corresponds to the Iranian fertility goddess Ardvi Sur Anahita.

summary.id: Satu pandangan: kultus Mokosh beralih ke Paraskeva.
summary.en: One view: Mokosh's cult passed to Paraskeva.

summary.id: Kajian lanjutan: kaitan Paraskeva dengan pemintalan, air, dan hari Jumat berakar Kristen, bukan pagan.
summary.en: Later studies: Paraskeva's link with spinning, water and Friday has Christian, not pagan, roots.

summary.id: Satu sumber: ia dewi yang melindungi pemintalan dan tenun.
summary.en: One source: she protected spinning and weaving.

summary.id: Sumber lain: data etimologi menunjukkan pemintalan bukan peran utamanya.
summary.en: Another source: etymology shows spinning was not her main role.

short_description.id: Mommotti adalah sosok penakut anak dalam tradisi Sardinia, lelaki bermantel hitam bertudung yang berkeliling rumah mencari anak nakal untuk dibawa pergi.
short_description.en: The mommotti is a Sardinian bogeyman, a man in a black hooded cloak who goes from house to house looking for naughty children to carry off.

long_description.id: Mommotti, juga bobbotti atau momotti, adalah sosok khayalan Sardinia untuk menakut-nakuti anak, mirip uomo nero atau raksasa jahat yang membawa pergi anak nakal. Ia lelaki berjanggut lebat bermantel hitam panjang bertudung, bertongkat berbonggol dan bersepatu bot usang, yang menguping dari rumah ke rumah; di sebagian Sardinia ia dikaitkan dengan iblis.
long_description.en: The mommotti, also bobbotti or momotti, is an imaginary Sardinian figure for scaring children, like the uomo nero or a wicked ogre who takes away naughty ones. He is a thick-bearded man in a long black hooded cloak, with a knotty stick and worn boots, who eavesdrops from house to house; in parts of Sardinia he is tied to the devil.

long_description.id: Asal namanya diperdebatkan: topeng Mamuthones yang menurut Raffaele Ballore berakar pra-Kristen, kisah perompak Arab bernama Mohammed di selatan, atau keluarga penculik Marotta dari Korsika di utara.
long_description.en: The origin of the name is disputed: the Mamuthones masks, which Raffaele Ballore thinks have pre-Christian roots, a tale of an Arab raider named Mohammed in the south, or the Marotta kidnapping family of Corsica in the north.

statement.id: Dalam tradisi Sardinia, mommotti (juga bobbotti, mommoti, momotti) adalah sosok khayalan untuk menakut-nakuti anak.
statement.en: In Sardinian tradition the mommotti (also bobbotti, mommoti, momotti) is an imaginary figure used to frighten children.

claims.quote: Talvolta viene associato all'uomo nero, oppure a un orco cattivo con il compito di portare via i bambini che non si comportano bene.

statement.id: Kadang ia dikaitkan dengan uomo nero atau raksasa jahat yang bertugas membawa pergi anak yang nakal.
statement.en: It is sometimes linked to the uomo nero or to a wicked ogre whose job is to carry off children who misbehave.

claims.quote: Viene solitamente descritto come un uomo vestito con un lungo mantello nero con cappuccio che cela gli occhi. Utilizza un nodoso bastone e porta un paio di scarponi neri e malconci.

statement.id: Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai lelaki bermantel hitam panjang bertudung yang menutupi matanya, membawa tongkat berbonggol, dan memakai sepatu bot hitam usang.
statement.en: It is usually described as a man in a long black hooded cloak hiding his eyes, with a knotty stick and a pair of battered black boots.

claims.quote: Ha una folta barba e se si riesce a vederlo senza cappuccio il suo sguardo è terrificante. Passa di casa in casa ascoltando se qualche bambino fa i capricci. In alcune zone della Sardegna viene associato al diavolo.

statement.id: Ia berjanggut lebat dan tatapannya menakutkan bila terlihat tanpa tudung; ia berkeliling dari rumah ke rumah mendengarkan anak yang rewel, dan di sebagian Sardinia ia dikaitkan dengan iblis.
statement.en: He has a thick beard and a terrifying stare if seen without his hood; he goes from house to house listening for naughty children, and in parts of Sardinia he is linked with the devil.

claims.quote: L'origine del nome potrebbe derivare da Mamuthones, una delle spaventose maschere nere tradizionali dell'isola di Sardegna e la cui tradizione ha origine incerta.

statement.id: Namanya mungkin berasal dari Mamuthones, salah satu topeng hitam tradisional Sardinia yang menakutkan, yang asal-usul tradisinya tidak pasti.
statement.en: The name may come from the Mamuthones, one of the frightening traditional black masks of Sardinia, whose tradition is of uncertain origin.

claims.quote: Secondo lo studioso Raffaele Ballore, tali maschere fanno presumere il loro radicamento in epoche e contesti precristiani.

statement.id: Menurut peneliti Raffaele Ballore, topeng-topeng itu menunjukkan akar pada masa dan konteks pra-Kristen.
statement.en: According to the scholar Raffaele Ballore, these masks suggest roots in pre-Christian times and contexts.

claims.quote: si credet chi bènzat dae su capu de zosso casteddàju, in ube sos arabos e sos piratas irrobàbant a s'ispìssu. Si còntat de unu tzertu Mohammed, arabu dae sa pedde nighedda, chi attaccabat sas biddas a de notte.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Sardinia, di Sardinia selatan yang sering dijarah orang Arab dan perompak, nama ini dikaitkan dengan kisah seorang Arab berkulit gelap bernama Mohammed yang menyerang desa pada malam hari.
statement.en: According to the Sardinian-language article, in southern Sardinia, often raided by Arabs and pirates, the name is linked to a tale of a dark-skinned Arab called Mohammed who attacked villages by night.

claims.quote: Un'atera orizine, custa borta de su capu de susu, est cussa de sa famìlia Marotta chi in Còssiga, in s'epoca napoliònica, fachìat parìtzos secuèstros politicos.

statement.id: Asal-usul lain, dari Sardinia utara, adalah keluarga Marotta di Korsika yang pada masa Napoleon melakukan banyak penculikan politik.
statement.en: Another origin, from northern Sardinia, is the Marotta family of Corsica, which carried out many political kidnappings in the Napoleonic era.

short_description.id: Moon Lake Monster, atau Moonie, adalah kriptid yang dilaporkan menghuni Moon Lake di kawasan pegunungan Uinta, Duchesne County, Utah, dan digambarkan sebagai makhluk besar gelap menyerupai ular.
short_description.en: The Moon Lake Monster, or Moonie, is a cryptid said to live in Moon Lake, high in the Uinta Mountains of Duchesne County, Utah, described as a large, dark, serpent-like creature.

long_description.id: Moon Lake Monster, yang akrab disebut Moonie, adalah kriptid yang dilaporkan menghuni Moon Lake di kawasan pegunungan Uinta, Duchesne County, Utah. Meski sering kalah tenar dibanding Bear Lake Monster, Moonie menjadi bagian tetap cerita rakyat setempat di High Uintas, dan warga mengatakan bahwa sudah bertahun-tahun makhluk ini dibicarakan.
long_description.en: The Moon Lake Monster, popularly called Moonie, is a cryptid said to live in Moon Lake, high in the Uinta Mountains of Duchesne County, Utah. Less famous than the Bear Lake Monster, Moonie nonetheless has a firm place in the local lore of the High Uintas, and locals say it has been talked about for years.

long_description.id: Legendanya berakar pada cerita rakyat setempat, termasuk kisah yang dikaitkan dengan orang Ute yang dahulu menghindari kawasan itu karena danau dianggap dihuni "roh air". Roh-roh itu dipercaya mampu menarik orang ke bawah permukaan. Menurut warga, orang Ute tidak mau mendekati danau karena takhayul tertentu, padahal reservasi mereka tak jauh dari sana.
long_description.en: The legend grows out of local lore, among it stories linked to the Ute, who in the past kept away from the area because the lake was thought to be inhabited by "water spirits". These spirits were believed able to pull people beneath the surface. According to locals, the Ute would not come near the lake out of certain superstitions, though their reservation lies close by.

long_description.id: Penampakan modern biasanya menggambarkan makhluk besar, gelap, menyerupai ular yang meninggalkan riak berbentuk V di permukaan air. Pada 1994 Bill Reardon, mantan pemilik Moon Lake Resort, melaporkan melihat riak yang bergerak zig-zag melintasi danau, sedangkan saksi lain menyamakannya dengan "batang kayu bergelombang" bersisik sepanjang 12 sampai 15 kaki.
long_description.en: Modern sightings usually describe a large, dark, serpent-like being leaving V-shaped wakes on the surface. In 1994 Bill Reardon, a former owner of the Moon Lake Resort, reported seeing a ripple zigzagging across the lake, while other witnesses likened it to a scaly "bumpy log" 12 to 15 feet long.

short_description.id: Mormo adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Yunani yang namanya dipakai untuk menakuti anak-anak agar tidak nakal.
short_description.en: Mormo was a female spirit of Greek folklore whose name was used to frighten children into behaving.

long_description.id: Mormo adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Yunani, yang namanya dipanggil ibu dan pengasuh untuk menakuti anak agar tidak nakal. Ia digolongkan sebagai momok sekelas Empusa dan Lamia. Bentuk jamaknya, mormones, berarti "yang menakutkan" atau "yang buruk rupa".
long_description.en: Mormo was a female spirit of Greek folklore; mothers and nurses called on her name to scare children out of misbehaving. She was counted as a bugbear of the same class as Empusa and Lamia. The plural form mormones means "fearful ones" or "hideous ones".

long_description.id: Dalam kutipan sebuah puisi, Mormo membuat anak-anak gemetar: kepalanya bertelinga besar, ia berjalan merangkak, dan berganti dari satu wajah ke wajah lain. Dalam kutipan sebuah lakon, seorang pembicara yang pusing melihat baju zirah menakutkan memohon agar "Mormo" disingkirkan, dan dalam kutipan lain orang diminta tidak takut mati seperti takut pada Mormolykeion, hantu penakut.
long_description.en: In a quoted poem the Mormo makes children tremble: on its head were huge ears, it walked on all fours, and it changed from one face to another. In a quoted play a speaker made dizzy by terrifying armor begs that the "Mormo" be taken away, and in another passage a listener is urged not to fear death as if it were a Mormolykeion, a hobgoblin.

long_description.id: Mormolyceion adalah momok yang sama dan dipakai untuk tujuan yang sama. Mormolyceia dikatakan dapat mengambil wujud wanita cantik untuk memikat pemuda ke ranjang, lalu menghisap darah dan memakan daging mereka. Sebuah catatan yang hanya berasal dari satu sumber menyebut Mormo asli adalah perempuan Korintus yang memakan anak-anaknya lalu terbang pergi.
long_description.en: The Mormolyceion is the same phantom or bugbear and was used for the same purpose. The Mormolyceia were also said to be capable of taking on the shape of beautiful women in order to draw young men to bed, where they drained their blood and ate their flesh. A report preserved in just one source holds that the first Mormo, a woman from Corinth, devoured her children and then flew away.

short_description.id: Mugwump, juga disebut Old Tessie, adalah monster danau yang konon tinggal di Lake Timiskaming di perbatasan Ontario dan Quebec, digambarkan berkepala kuda dan bertubuh ular.
short_description.en: The Mugwump, also called Old Tessie, is a lake monster said to live in Lake Timiskaming on the Ontario–Quebec border, pictured with a horse's head and a serpent's body.

long_description.id: Mugwump, juga dikenal sebagai Old Tessie atau Monster of Lake Temiscamingue, adalah monster danau yang konon tinggal di Lake Timiskaming, di perbatasan provinsi Ontario dan Quebec. Danau itu dikatakan menjadi rumah bagi makhluk berkepala kuda dan bertubuh ular.
long_description.en: The Mugwump, also known as Old Tessie or the Monster of Lake Temiscamingue, is a lake monster said to live in Lake Timiskaming, on the border of the provinces of Ontario and Quebec. The lake is said to be home to a creature with a horse's head and a serpent's body.

long_description.id: Namanya berasal dari kata Algonquin yang makna pastinya tidak jelas; pada 1979 Wali Kota New Liskeard Jack Dent melaporkan bahwa artinya "sturgeon pemberani". Menurut narasumber Dent, panjang mugwump setara empat orang pejuang pribumi, sehingga diperkirakan lebih dari 20 kaki. Tulisan Dent di North Bay Nugget pada 20 April 1979 adalah dokumentasi tertulis pertama tentang makhluk ini.
long_description.en: Its name comes from an Algonquin word of unclear meaning; in 1979 New Liskeard mayor Jack Dent reported that it meant "fearless sturgeon". According to Dent's informant, the mugwump was as long as four Indigenous warriors, probably over 20 feet. Dent's piece in the North Bay Nugget on 20 April 1979 is the first written documentation of the creature.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan akan makhluk gaib di danau itu lebih tua. Dalam perjalanan kano tahun 1879, voyageur Sha-Ka-Nash mencatat para pemandu Anishinaabe-nya mempersembahkan tembakau di tempat seperti Devil's Rock kepada makhluk gaib penghuni danau, persembahan yang dianggap penting untuk meraih kemurahan roh air itu. Penjelasan modern yang paling umum adalah bahwa Mugwump sebenarnya ikan sturgeon besar.
long_description.en: Belief in a supernatural being in the lake is older. On an 1879 canoe voyage, the voyageur Sha-Ka-Nash recorded his Anishinaabe guides offering tobacco at places such as Devil's Rock to an otherworldly creature living in the lake, an offering thought advisable to court the water sprite's favour. The most common modern explanation is that the Mugwump is a large sturgeon.

short_description.id: Mulher marinha adalah putri duyung berkaki kambing dalam legenda Portugis yang dalam tradisi Azores menikahi lelaki darat dan membawa keberuntungan.
short_description.en: The mulher marinha is a goat-footed mermaid of Portuguese legend who in Azorean tradition marries a man of the land and brings good fortune.

long_description.id: Mulher marinha adalah makhluk mitos dalam legenda dan tradisi rakyat Portugis, semacam putri duyung berkaki kambing: dari pinggang ke bawah ia bersisik, dengan kaki kambing dan sirip di tungkainya. Ia dikaitkan dengan mouras encantadas, Nereid, dan Oceanid.
long_description.en: The mulher marinha is a mythical being of Portuguese legend and folk tradition, a kind of goat-footed mermaid: scaly from the waist down, with goat's feet and fins on her legs. She is associated with the enchanted mouras, Nereids and Oceanids.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Kepulauan Azores, ia keluar dari air, menjelma perempuan, dan menikahi petani atau nelayan, membawakan kebahagiaan, kesuburan, dan keberuntungan.
long_description.en: In Azorean tradition she leaves the water, becomes a woman and marries a farmer or fisherman, bringing joy, fertility and fortune.

long_description.id: Livro de Linhagens do Conde Dom Pedro memuat kisah Dona Marinha: seorang ksatria berkuda di tepi laut menemukan seorang perempuan laut tidur di pantai, membaptisnya, dan menamainya Marinha karena ia keluar dari laut. Perempuan itu tidak pernah berbicara sampai suatu hari, karena cemas akan anaknya, ia berteriak dan sepotong daging keluar dari mulutnya; sejak itu ia bisa berbicara.
long_description.en: The Livro de Linhagens do Conde Dom Pedro contains the tale of Dona Marinha: a knight riding by the sea found a sea woman asleep on the shore, had her baptised and named her Marinha because she had come out of the sea. She never spoke until one day, fearing for her son, she cried out and a piece of flesh came out of her mouth; from then on she could speak.

long_description.id: Versi yang dicatat di Açores menyebutnya putri laut yang ditemukan D. Froião sedang tidur. Dari pernikahan mereka lahir keluarga Marinhos, dan salah satu anaknya, Machico, disebut menemukan Madeira.
long_description.en: A version recorded in the Azores (Açores) calls her a daughter of the sea whom D. Froião found asleep. Their marriage produced the Marinhos family, and one of the sons, Machico, is said to have discovered Madeira.

short_description.id: Mungoon-Gali atau Mungoongarlee adalah biawak goanna raksasa berbisa dalam cerita rakyat Yuwaalaraay [mungoon-gali-c01].
short_description.en: Mungoon-Gali or Mungoongarlee is a venomous giant goanna in Yuwaalaraay folklore [mungoon-gali-c01].

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Yuwaalaraay, Mungoon-Gali (juga dieja Mungoongarlee) adalah sosok biawak goanna raksasa yang meneror penduduk dengan gigitan berbisa dan nafsu makan besar [mungoon-gali-c01]. Pada zaman dahulu, dikisahkan bahwa biawaklah yang memiliki bisa, bukan ular [mungoon-gali-c02].
long_description.en: In Yuwaalaraay folklore, Mungoon-Gali (also transcribed Mungoongarlee) is a giant goanna who plagued communities with toxic bites and an enormous appetite [mungoon-gali-c01]. In ancient times, lore recounts that lizards possessed venom rather than snakes [mungoon-gali-c02].

long_description.id: Ular hitam Ouyouboolooey kemudian menipu Mungoon-Gali untuk menyerahkan kantung bisanya [mungoon-gali-c03], lalu membawanya kabur ke dalam semak belukar sehingga bangsa ular menjadi berbisa dan goanna kehilangan gigitan mematikannya [mungoon-gali-c04].
long_description.en: Ouyouboolooey the black snake tricked Mungoon-Gali into relinquishing his venom sac [mungoon-gali-c03], escaping into the bush and causing snakes to become venomous while goannas lost their lethal bite [mungoon-gali-c04].

long_description.id: Dalam kumpulan cerita yang lebih tua, Mungoongarlee digambarkan sebagai iguana terbesar yang panjangnya sekitar lima kaki dari lidah hingga ekor bahkan dalam wujudnya yang lebih kecil sekarang, dan menjadi teror di negeri itu karena gigitannya beracun. Pada masa itu gigitan ular tidak beracun, tetapi gigitan iguana beracun. Kerusakan yang ia timbulkan begitu besar sehingga semua suku lain mengadakan pertemuan untuk membahas cara menghentikan pembantaian itu.
long_description.en: In an older collection of tales, Mungoongarlee is described as the largest kind of iguana, about five feet from tongue to tail even in his smaller present form, and a terror in the land because of his poisonous bite. In those days a snake's bite was not poisonous but an iguana's was. The havoc he caused was so great that all the other tribes held a meeting to discuss how to stop the slaughter.

long_description.id: Menurut kisah itu, sejak peristiwa tersebut ularlah yang beracun, bukan iguana, dan terjadi permusuhan antara keduanya yang tak pernah bertemu tanpa berkelahi. Mungoongarlee adalah wirreenun yang hebat dan mengetahui tanaman yang jika dimakan setelah gigitan ular membuat racunnya tak mampu membunuh atau melukai.
long_description.en: In the story, ever since then it is the snakes that are poisonous and not the iguanas, and the two have been in feud, never meeting without fighting. Mungoongarlee was a great wirreenun and knew of a plant that, eaten after a snakebite, made the poison powerless to kill or injure.

short_description.id: Na Ruixa adalah peri air dari Kepulauan Balears yang konon tinggal di gua Mallorca dan menangkap pelaut dengan mantel birunya saat badai.
short_description.en: Na Ruixa is a water fairy of the Balearic Islands said to live in caves on Mallorca and catch sailors in storms with her blue cloak.

long_description.id: Na Ruixa atau Ruixa Mantells adalah peri dari mitologi Balears yang mungkin berakar pada tradisi lisan setempat. Ia konon tinggal di gua-gua Mallorca, mungkin di teluk Pollença, dan memakai mantel biru lebar untuk menangkap pelaut lengah di tengah badai.
long_description.en: Na Ruixa or Ruixa Mantells is a fairy of Balearic mythology possibly rooted in local oral tradition. She is said to live in caves on Mallorca, perhaps in the bay of Pollença, and wears a wide blue cloak to capture unwary sailors in storms.

long_description.id: Sosoknya pertama kali digambarkan dalam sastra oleh Miquel Costa i Llobera dalam Tradicions i fantasies (1903), lalu dipopulerkan oleh penyanyi Maria del Mar Bonet.
long_description.en: She was first described in literature by Miquel Costa i Llobera in Tradicions i fantasies (1903) and later popularised by Maria del Mar Bonet.

long_description.id: Sebuah kajian di Boletín de la Real Academia Española melukiskannya jahat sekaligus cantik, seperti peri dari Pirineos. Dalam sajak Miquel Costa i Llobera yang dinyanyikan Maria del Mar Bonet, Na Ruixa-mantells merenggut seorang kekasih di tengah angin kencang.
long_description.en: An essay in the Boletín de la Real Academia Española paints her as malign yet beautiful, like a fairy of the Pyrenees. In Miquel Costa i Llobera's poem, sung by Maria del Mar Bonet, Na Ruixa-mantells seizes a lover in a strong gale.

long_description.id: Penceritaan ulang Imma Villegas menggambarkannya sebagai peri cantik berambut pirang seperti benang emas. Dengan suaranya yang merdu ia memikat pelaut yang nekat berlayar dalam cuaca buruk dan menyeret mereka ke istananya di dasar laut, yang bertiang karang merah.
long_description.en: Imma Villegas's retelling pictures her as a beautiful fairy with hair like a thread of gold. With her melodious voice she enchants sailors who brave bad weather and drags them to her palace at the bottom of the sea, with columns of red coral.

short_description.id: Nemty adalah dewa Mesir kuno yang dipuja di Antaeopolis di Mesir Hulu, kemudian dikenal sebagai dewa penyeberang yang digambarkan sebagai elang di atas perahu.
short_description.en: Nemty is an ancient Egyptian god worshipped at Antaeopolis in Upper Egypt, later known as the god of ferrymen and shown as a falcon on a boat.

long_description.id: Nemty adalah dewa Mesir yang pemujaannya berpusat di Antaeopolis di bagian utara Mesir Hulu. Pemujaannya sangat tua: pada Dinasti Kedua ia sudah memiliki pendeta, dan ia muncul pada palet upacara dari zaman Naqada II dan III. Pada awalnya ia tampaknya pelindung kawasan Badari, tetapi karena informasi yang bertahan sedikit, tidak banyak diketahui fungsi aslinya atau apakah ia lebih dari sekadar gelar Horus.
long_description.en: Nemty is an Egyptian god whose worship centred on Antaeopolis in the northern part of Upper Egypt. His worship is very old: by the Second Dynasty he already had priests, and he appears on ceremonial palettes of the Naqada II and III periods. He originally appears to have been patron of the area around Badari, but because little information survives, his original function, or whether he was more than a title of Horus, is not well known.

long_description.id: Seiring waktu Nemty dipandang sebagai dewa para tukang perahu, digambarkan sebagai elang di atas perahu yang merujuk pada Horus. Sebagai dewa penyeberang ia menyandang gelar Nemty, yang berarti "(ia yang) bepergian". Ia juga dianggap sebagai tukang perahu alam baka yang mengangkut jiwa orang yang meninggal menyeberangi sungai alam baka.
long_description.en: In time Nemty came to be seen as the god of ferrymen, shown as a falcon perched on a boat in allusion to Horus. In that role he took the title Nemty, which means "(one who) travels". He was also regarded as the ferryman of the afterlife who carried the souls of the dead across the river of the underworld.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Contendings of Horus and Seth, Seth menyuruh Nemty tidak menyeberangkan siapa pun yang mirip Isis, tetapi Isis menyamar sebagai perempuan tua dan Nemty menyeberangkannya setelah dibayar sebuah cincin emas. Dua firaun Dinasti Keenam memiliki nama yang memuat nama Nemty. Pembacaan lama nama dewa ini sebagai Anti atau Anty dinyatakan keliru oleh sejumlah studi.
long_description.en: In the tale of the Contendings of Horus and Seth, Seth instructs Nemty not to ferry anyone resembling Isis, but Isis disguises herself as an old woman and Nemty takes her across after being paid a gold ring. Two Sixth Dynasty pharaohs bore names incorporating Nemty's. The older reading of the god's name as Anti or Anty has been shown to be incorrect by several studies.

statement.en: Over time Nemty became considered the god of ferrymen and was depicted as a falcon standing on a boat, a reference to Horus; his later cult centre was in Antaeopolis and also in Per-Nemty (House of Nemty) in the 12th Upper Egyptian nome.

short_description.id: Niemotsu no Ko adalah dewa bumi Yamato yang dicatat dalam Kojiki serta Nihon Shoki.
short_description.en: Niemotsu no Ko is an earthly deity of Yamato recorded in Kojiki and Nihon Shoki.

long_description.id: Niemotsu no Ko adalah dewa bumi Yamato yang dicatat dalam Kojiki serta Nihon Shoki. Nihon Shoki memakai bentuk penulisan namanya yang berbeda, dan ia merupakan leluhur pemelihara kormoran Ada.
long_description.en: Niemotsu no Ko is an earthly deity of Yamato recorded in Kojiki and Nihon Shoki. The Nihon Shoki uses a different written form of his name, and he is ancestor of Ada’s cormorant keepers.

long_description.id: Unsur nie mengacu pada upeti makanan yang dipakai penguasa untuk menegaskan kepemilikan. Namanya ditafsirkan sebagai orang yang membawa makanan persembahan kepada dewa atau kaisar.
long_description.en: The nie element refers to food tribute through which rulers confirmed possession. His name is interpreted as a person bearing food offered to a god or emperor.

long_description.id: Ia adalah dewa pertama yang ditemui Kamuyamato-iwarebiko, yang dipandu Yatagarasu, di hilir sungai Yoshino; ia sedang menangkap ikan dengan bubu dan menyebut dirinya dewa bumi. Sungai Yoshino terkenal dengan ikan ayu, dan upeti para pemelihara kormoran Ada kepada istana diduga juga ikan ayu; mereka juga dinilai berhubungan dengan kelompok Kume. Karena Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki tidak menggambarkannya sebagai penentang, para ahli menduga ia tidak melawan kekuasaan Yamato atau tunduk sangat awal.
long_description.en: He is the first deity met by Kamuyamato-iwarebiko, guided by Yatagarasu, at the lower Yoshino River; he was catching fish with a fish trap and called himself an earthly deity. The Yoshino River is famed for ayu, and the tribute of Ada's cormorant keepers to the court is thought to have been ayu too; they are also thought to have been linked with the Kume group. Because the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki do not depict him as a resister, scholars suggest he did not resist the Yamato kingship or submitted very early.

claims.quote: 八咫烏に先導された神倭伊波礼毘古命が、吉野川の川尻で最初に出会った神。筌で魚を捕っており、神倭伊波礼毘古命が尋ねると国つ神を称した。

statement.id: Ia adalah dewa pertama yang ditemui Kamuyamato-iwarebiko (神倭伊波礼毘古命), yang dipandu Yatagarasu (八咫烏), di hilir sungai Yoshino (吉野川); ia sedang menangkap ikan dengan bubu dan, saat ditanya, menyebut dirinya dewa bumi (国つ神).
statement.en: He is the first deity met by Kamuyamato-iwarebiko (神倭伊波礼毘古命), guided by Yatagarasu (八咫烏), at the lower Yoshino River (吉野川); he was catching fish with a fish trap and, when asked, called himself an earthly deity (国つ神).

claims.quote: 吉野川は鮎の名産地として知られ、阿陀之鵜養が朝廷に貢上したニヘも鮎とみられる。また久米歌では「鵜養が伴」のことが歌われており、この「鵜養の伴」が阿陀之鵜養と考えられることから、阿陀之鵜養は来目部と関係を有していたことが指摘されている。

statement.id: Sungai Yoshino terkenal dengan ikan ayu, dan upeti (nie) para pemelihara kormoran Ada (阿陀之鵜養) kepada istana diduga juga ikan ayu; karena lagu Kume (久米歌) menyebut "rombongan pemelihara kormoran", mereka dinilai berhubungan dengan kelompok Kume (来目部).
statement.en: The Yoshino River is famed for ayu, and the tribute (nie) of the cormorant keepers of Ada (阿陀之鵜養) to the court is thought to have been ayu; since the Kume songs (久米歌) mention a "band of cormorant keepers", they are thought to have been linked with the Kume group (来目部).

claims.quote: ただし贄持之子は記紀に反抗者や敵対者としての描かれておらず、そのため倭王権に対して無抵抗であったか、あるいはきわめて早い段階で帰順した可能性が指摘されている。

statement.id: Karena Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki (記紀) tidak menggambarkannya sebagai penentang, para ahli menduga ia tidak melawan kekuasaan Yamato (倭王権) atau tunduk sangat awal.
statement.en: Because the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki (記紀) do not depict him as a resister, scholars suggest he did not resist the Yamato kingship (倭王権) or submitted very early.

short_description.id: Nightmarchers (huakaʻi pō) adalah hantu prajurit Hawaii kuno yang mematikan dan berbaris pada malam keramat sebagai pengawal depan raja atau kepala suku yang suci.
short_description.en: Nightmarchers (huakaʻi pō) are the deadly ghosts of ancient Hawaiian warriors who march on sacred nights as the vanguard of a sacred king or chief.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Hawaii, Nightmarchers (huakaʻi pō) atau "Barisan roh" (ʻoiʻo) adalah hantu prajurit suku Hawaii kuno yang mematikan, pengawal depan bagi raja, kepala suku, atau kepala suku perempuan yang suci. Sebuah kajian mitologi Hawaii menyebutnya "Pejalan malam" dan "Barisan roh", arak-arakan dewa dan roh yang datang pada malam keramat untuk mengunjungi tempat suci atau menyambut kerabat yang sekarat. Sumber lain juga menulis bahwa kepala suku tinggi dan prajurit berbaris berbondong-bondong dengan tombak.
long_description.en: Hawaiian myth knows the Nightmarchers (huakaʻi pō), also called "Spirit ranks" (ʻoiʻo), as lethal phantoms of long-dead tribal warriors who go ahead of a sacred king, chief or chiefess. A study of Hawaiian mythology renders the names as "Marchers of the night" and "Spirit ranks" and describes processions of gods and spirits visiting sacred places on sacred nights or welcoming a dying relative. Another collection likewise has high chiefs and warriors marching in crowds with spears.

long_description.id: Pada malam Kāne, Kū, Lono, atau Kanaloa mereka konon keluar dari makam atau bangkit dari laut lalu berbaris dalam rombongan besar menuju medan perang kuno atau tempat suci, terus berjalan dari matahari terbenam sampai menjelang fajar. Para pejalan berukuran biasa, berpakaian perang atau busana kepala suku atau dewa, membawa tombak dan pentungan; sebagian menabuh genderang dan meniup kerang. Mereka melayang, kakinya tak menyentuh air atau tanah, dan tak meninggalkan bukti. Arak-arakan dewa berjalan lima sejajar dengan lima obor merah; arak-arakan kepala suku diiringi aumakua, berjalan diam atau dengan genderang, seruling hidung, dan nyanyian. Dewi Hiʻiaka sering ada di antara mereka.
long_description.en: On the nights of Kāne, Kū, Lono or Kanaloa they are said to emerge from burial sites or rise from the sea and march in a large group to ancient battle sites or sacred places, keeping on from sunset until shortly before sunrise. The marchers are of normal size, dressed for battle or in the costume of chiefs or gods, carrying spears and clubs; some beat drums and blow conch shells. They hover, their feet touching neither water nor ground, and leave no evidence. Processions of gods go five abreast with five red torches; processions of chiefs are accompanied by aumakua and go silently or with drum, nose-flute and chanting. The goddess Hiʻiaka is often among them.

long_description.id: Bertemu mereka berbahaya: manusia yang memandang atau terlihat melawan mereka konon mati secara kejam, dan bagian tubuh keramat penguasa tidak boleh dilihat, dengan hukuman mati seketika oleh cahaya dan panas dari mata prajurit. Tanda kedekatan mereka adalah bau seperti kematian dan obor yang makin terang, serta nyanyian dan tabuhan dari malam hari. Mereka juga bisa muncul pada siang hari untuk mengantar kerabat yang sekarat ke dunia roh.
long_description.en: Meeting them is dangerous: a mortal who looks upon them or is seen defying them is said to die violently, and sacred parts of a ruler's body must not be seen, the penalty being instant death by light and heat from the warriors' eyes. Signs of their approach are a death-like odor and torches growing brighter, along with chanting and drumming in the night. They may also appear by day to escort a dying relative to the spirit world.

long_description.id: Ada beberapa cara selamat. Sebagian orang berpendapat bahwa berbaring diam telungkup menunjukkan hormat; sumber lain menyarankan melepas pakaian dan telentang berpura-pura tidur. Manusia luput bila leluhur di antara pejalan mengenalinya dan berseru "Naʻu!" ("milikku"), atau bila kerabat atau aumakuanya hadir melindungi. Menanam semak ti hidup di sekitar rumah konon membuat huakaʻi pō menghindari daerah itu.
long_description.en: There are several ways to survive. Some say lying motionless face down shows respect; another source advises removing clothing and turning face up to feign sleep. A person escapes if an ancestor among the marchers recognizes him and cries "Naʻu!" ("mine"), or if a relative or his aumakua is present to protect him. Planting living ti shrubs around the home is said to make the huakaʻi pō avoid the area.

long_description.id: Dalam budaya populer, Nightmarchers muncul dalam episode "Belle" serial Lilo & Stitch: The Series dan dalam film Netflix Finding ʻOhana.
long_description.en: In popular culture, Nightmarchers appear in the "Belle" episode of Lilo & Stitch: The Series and in the Netflix film Finding ʻOhana.

claims.quote: In Hawaiian mythology, Nightmarchers (huakaʻi pō) or Spirit Ranks (ʻoiʻo) are the deadly ghosts of ancient tribal Hawaiian warriors.

statement.id: Nightmarchers adalah arwah mematikan prajurit kuno suku Hawaii.
statement.en: Nightmarchers are deadly ghosts of ancient tribal Hawaiian warriors.

claims.quote: The nightmarchers are the vanguard for a sacred king, chief, or chiefess.

statement.id: Nightmarchers bertindak sebagai garda pengawal untuk raja atau kepala suku yang suci.
statement.en: The nightmarchers serve as the vanguard for a sacred ruler or noble.

claims.quote: They march in darkness after sunset and march as a group continuously until just before sunrise.

statement.id: Mereka berbaris berkelompok di kegelapan malam sejak matahari terbenam hingga menjelang fajar.
statement.en: They march in group formation throughout the night from sunset until sunrise.

claims.quote: On the nights honoring the Hawaiian gods Kāne, Kū, Lono, or on the nights of Kanaloa, they are said to come forth from their burial sites or to rise up from the ocean, and to march in a large group to ancient Hawaiian battle sites or other sacred places.

statement.id: Pada malam yang menghormati dewa Hawaii Kāne, Kū, Lono, atau pada malam Kanaloa, mereka konon keluar dari makam atau muncul dari laut dan berbaris dalam rombongan besar menuju medan perang kuno atau tempat suci lain.
statement.en: On the nights honoring the Hawaiian gods Kāne, Kū, Lono, or on the nights of Kanaloa, they are said to come forth from their burial sites or rise up from the ocean and march in a large group to ancient battle sites or other sacred places.

claims.quote: The legend says the night marchers are normal-size warriors, dressed for battle, carrying spears, clubs, and some are beating war drums and blowing tones from conch shells, to announce the advancing of their march.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, para pejalan malam adalah prajurit berukuran biasa yang berpakaian perang, membawa tombak dan pentungan; sebagian menabuh genderang perang dan meniup kerang untuk mengumumkan barisan mereka.
statement.en: The legend says the night marchers are normal-size warriors dressed for battle, carrying spears and clubs; some beat war drums and blow conch shells to announce their march.

claims.quote: According to the myth, they are suspended in air; their feet do not touch water or ground as they traverse through the night, and they leave no evidence of their visitations.

statement.id: Menurut mitos, mereka melayang di udara; kaki mereka tidak menyentuh air atau tanah saat melintasi malam, dan mereka tidak meninggalkan bukti kunjungan.
statement.en: According to the myth they are suspended in air; their feet touch neither water nor ground as they cross the night, and they leave no evidence of their visits.

claims.quote: Ancient Hawaiian beliefs state that any mortal looking upon or being seen in defiance toward the marchers will die violently.

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan Hawaii kuno, setiap manusia yang memandang atau terlihat melawan para pejalan itu akan mati secara kejam.
statement.en: According to ancient Hawaiian belief, any mortal who looks upon the marchers or is seen in defiance of them will die violently.

claims.quote: Some people maintain that if the mortal lies motionless, face down on the ground, they are showing proper respect, fear, and deference to the night marchers, and they will be spared.

statement.id: Sebagian orang berpendapat bahwa manusia yang berbaring diam telungkup di tanah menunjukkan hormat, takut, dan tunduk kepada para pejalan malam sehingga akan dibiarkan.
statement.en: Some maintain that a mortal who lies motionless face down on the ground shows proper respect, fear and deference to the night marchers and will be spared.

claims.quote: Additionally, mortals can avoid harm or death from night marchers by being fortunate to have an ancient ancestor marcher present to recognize them. As they encounter the mortal, they will call out "Naʻu!", which means "mine" in Hawaiian.

statement.id: Manusia juga dapat luput dari bahaya bila ada leluhur kuno di antara para pejalan yang mengenalinya; saat bertemu, mereka berseru "Naʻu!", yang berarti "milikku" dalam bahasa Hawaii.
statement.en: Mortals can also escape harm if an ancient ancestor among the marchers recognizes them; on meeting the mortal they call out "Naʻu!", meaning "mine" in Hawaiian.

claims.quote: Legend says planting living ti (Cordyline sp.) shrubs around one's home is said to keep away all evil spirits and will cause the huakaʻi pō to avoid the area.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, menanam semak ti (Cordyline) hidup di sekeliling rumah menangkal semua roh jahat dan membuat huakaʻi pō menghindari daerah itu.
statement.en: Legend says planting living ti (Cordyline) shrubs around one's home keeps away all evil spirits and makes the huakaʻi pō avoid the area.

claims.quote: The following signs are a foul and musky “death-like” odor, and torches getting brighter and brighter as the night marchers get closer.

statement.id: Tanda-tandanya adalah bau apek dan busuk seperti kematian serta obor yang makin terang saat para pejalan malam mendekat.
statement.en: The signs are a foul, musky "death-like" odor and torches growing brighter as the night marchers draw closer.

claims.quote: Nightmarchers might appear during the day if they are to escort a dying relative to the spirit world.

statement.id: Para pejalan malam bisa muncul pada siang hari bila mereka hendak mengantar kerabat yang sekarat ke dunia roh.
statement.en: Nightmarchers might appear during the day if they are to escort a dying relative to the spirit world.

claims.quote: In ancient Hawaiian lore, the laws declared body parts of a King or Chief to be sacred, and not to be seen by a mortal. The punishment for looking at these parts is always instant death, usually by bolts of intense light and flaming heat originating from several of the warrior's eyes aimed toward the mortal.

statement.id: Dalam tradisi Hawaii kuno, bagian tubuh raja atau kepala suku dinyatakan keramat dan tidak boleh dilihat manusia; hukuman bagi yang memandangnya selalu kematian seketika, biasanya oleh berkas cahaya dan panas menyala dari beberapa mata prajurit yang diarahkan kepada manusia itu.
statement.en: In ancient Hawaiian lore the body parts of a King or Chief were sacred and not to be seen by a mortal; the punishment for looking at them is always instant death, usually by bolts of intense light and flaming heat from several of the warrior's eyes aimed at the mortal.

claims.quote: The Goddess named Hiʻiaka-i-ka-poli-o-Pele, (commonly shortened to Hiʻiaka), is often within the night marchers.

statement.id: Dewi bernama Hiʻiaka-i-ka-poli-o-Pele (biasa disingkat Hiʻiaka) sering berada di antara para pejalan malam.
statement.en: The goddess named Hiʻiaka-i-ka-poli-o-Pele (commonly shortened to Hiʻiaka) is often among the night marchers.

claims.quote: In the 2005 Lilo & Stitch: The Series episode "Belle", Lilo Pelekai seeks to prove that Nightmarchers exist. Nightmarchers are also featured in the 2021 Netflix film Finding ʻOhana.

statement.id: Dalam episode "Belle" serial Lilo & Stitch: The Series (2005), Lilo Pelekai berusaha membuktikan bahwa Nightmarchers ada; Nightmarchers juga muncul dalam film Netflix Finding ʻOhana (2021).
statement.en: In the 2005 Lilo & Stitch: The Series episode "Belle", Lilo Pelekai seeks to prove Nightmarchers exist; they also feature in the 2021 Netflix film Finding ʻOhana.

claims.quote: Especially is this true of the processions of gods and spirits who come on certain sacred nights to visit the sacred places, or to welcome a dying relative and conduct him to the aumakua world.
claims.locator: Chapter X, The Soul After Death

statement.id: Arak-arakan dewa dan roh datang pada malam-malam keramat tertentu untuk mengunjungi tempat suci atau menyambut kerabat yang sekarat dan menuntunnya ke dunia aumakua.
statement.en: Processions of gods and spirits come on certain sacred nights to visit the sacred places or to welcome a dying relative and conduct him to the aumakua world.

claims.quote: "Marchers of the night" (Huaka‘i-po) or "Spirit ranks" (Oi‘o) they are called.
claims.locator: Chapter X, The Soul After Death

statement.id: Arak-arakan itu disebut "Pejalan malam" (Huakaʻi-pō) atau "Barisan roh" (Oiʻo).
statement.en: The processions are called "Marchers of the night" (Huakaʻi-pō) or "Spirit ranks" (Oiʻo).

claims.quote: Always, if seen, the marchers are dressed according to ancient usage in the costume of chiefs or of gods. If the procession is one of gods, the marchers move five abreast with five torches burning red between the ranks, and without music save that of the voice raised in chant.
claims.locator: Chapter X, The Soul After Death

statement.id: Bila terlihat, para pejalan selalu berpakaian ala adat kuno, yaitu busana kepala suku atau dewa; jika arak-arakan dewa, mereka berbaris lima sejajar dengan lima obor merah di antara barisan dan hanya diiringi nyanyian.
statement.en: When seen, the marchers are always dressed in ancient fashion in the costume of chiefs or of gods; if the procession is one of gods, they move five abreast with five red torches between the ranks, accompanied only by chanting.

claims.quote: Processions of chiefs are accompanied by aumakua and march in silence, or to the accompaniment of drum, nose-flute, and chanting.
claims.locator: Chapter X, The Soul After Death

statement.id: Arak-arakan kepala suku diiringi aumakua dan berjalan dalam diam atau diiringi genderang, seruling hidung, dan nyanyian.
statement.en: Processions of chiefs are accompanied by aumakua and march in silence or to the accompaniment of drum, nose-flute and chanting.

claims.quote: They are seen on the sacred nights of Ku, Lono, Kane, or Kanaloa, or they may be seen by day if it is a procession to welcome the soul of a dying relative.
claims.locator: Chapter X, The Soul After Death

statement.id: Mereka terlihat pada malam keramat Ku, Lono, Kane, atau Kanaloa, atau pada siang hari bila arak-arakan itu menyambut jiwa kerabat yang sekarat.
statement.en: They are seen on the sacred nights of Ku, Lono, Kane or Kanaloa, or by day if the procession welcomes the soul of a dying relative.

claims.quote: To meet such a procession is very dangerous. "O-ia" (Let him be pierced) is the cry of the leader and if no relative among the dead or none of his aumakua is present to protect him, a ghostly spearsman will strike him dead. The wise thing to do is to "remove all clothing and turn face up and feign sleep."
claims.locator: Chapter X, The Soul After Death

statement.id: Bertemu arak-arakan itu sangat berbahaya: pemimpinnya berseru "O-ia" ("Biarlah ia ditusuk"), dan bila tak ada kerabat di antara orang mati atau aumakuanya yang melindungi, seorang penombak hantu akan membunuhnya; yang bijak adalah "melepas semua pakaian dan telentang berpura-pura tidur".
statement.en: Meeting such a procession is very dangerous: the leader cries "O-ia" ("Let him be pierced"), and if no dead relative or aumakua is present to protect him, a ghostly spearsman strikes him dead; the wise course is to "remove all clothing and turn face up and feign sleep".

claims.quote: Many Hawaiians and even some persons of foreign blood have seen this spirit march or heard the "chanting voices, the high notes of the flute, and drumming so loud as to seem beaten upon the side of the house."
claims.locator: Chapter X, The Soul After Death

statement.id: Banyak orang Hawaii, bahkan beberapa orang berdarah asing, mengaku pernah melihat arak-arakan roh ini atau mendengar "suara orang bernyanyi, nada tinggi seruling, dan tabuhan yang begitu keras seolah dipukul di dinding rumah".
statement.en: Many Hawaiians, and even some persons of foreign blood, have seen this spirit march or heard the "chanting voices, the high notes of the flute, and drumming so loud as to seem beaten upon the side of the house".

claims.quote: The high chiefs and warriors are supposed to march and go in crowds, carrying their spears and piercing those they met unless some ghost recognized that one and called to the others, "Alia [wait]," but if the word was "O-i-o [throw the spear]!" then that spirit's spear would strike death to the passer-by.
claims.locator: Section on ghosts and ancestor ghost-gods

statement.id: Kepala suku tinggi dan prajurit konon berbaris berbondong-bondong membawa tombak dan menusuk orang yang mereka temui, kecuali ada hantu yang mengenali orang itu dan berseru "Alia [tunggu]"; bila yang diserukan "O-i-o [lemparkan tombak]!", tombak roh itu membawa kematian bagi si pejalan.
statement.en: High chiefs and warriors are supposed to march in crowds carrying spears and piercing those they met, unless some ghost recognized the person and called "Alia [wait]"; if the word was "O-i-o [throw the spear]!" that spirit's spear brought death to the passer-by.

claims.quote: Barriers placed in the path of night marchers will not deter them.

statement.id: Rintangan yang dipasang di jalur para pejalan malam tidak akan menghalangi mereka.
statement.en: Barriers placed in the path of night marchers will not deter them.

SETTING: night Hawaiian lava-rock shoreline, dark ocean and further ranks behind, procession rising from ocean toward sacred sites [c04]. short_description.id: Nonell de la neu adalah raksasa salju dalam mitologi Katalan, pemuda yang menjadi anjing putih raksasa, membawa salju, dan melindungi kawanan ternak.
short_description.en: Nonell de la neu is a snow giant of Catalan mythology, a youth turned into a giant white dog who brings the snow and protects the flocks.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Katalan, Nonell de la neu adalah semacam raksasa salju. Dulunya ia pemuda tampan berjanggut lebat dan berambut pirang panjang, yang kemudian berubah menjadi anjing putih besar seukuran kuda. Ia muncul tak lama setelah salju pertama, karena dialah yang membawa salju dari satu tempat ke tempat lain.
long_description.en: In Catalan mythology Nonell de la neu is a kind of snow giant. Once a handsome youth with a thick beard and long blond hair, he became a great white dog the size of a horse. He appears soon after the first snowfall, since he carries the snow from place to place.

long_description.id: Ia dianggap damai: ternak tidur tenang saat ia mendekat karena tahu Nonell melindungi mereka. Tokoh ini berkerabat dengan Basajaun dari Basque dan mirip Yeti; Joan Amades mencatat satu versi legendanya di La Pobla de Lillet.
long_description.en: He is considered peaceful: flocks sleep easily when he comes near, knowing Nonell protects them. The figure is related to the Basque Basajaun and resembles the Yeti; Joan Amades recorded a version of the legend at La Pobla de Lillet.

long_description.id: Majalah El Temps juga memasukkan Nonell ke golongan raksasa dalam daftar tokoh mitologi daerah setempat, bersama Puigmal dan Caramançó.
long_description.en: The magazine El Temps also places the Nonell among the giants in its list of local mythological figures, together with the Puigmal and the Caramançó.
